tess: Ran the nightly perf job with continuous-batching enabled and saw steady memory growth on long-context workloads (~64k tokens). Not sure if it's kv cache fragmentation or a merge path bug.
raj: Ugh, saw similar in canary earlier today. Latency spikes when batches merge with different KV shapes. Did you capture a heap profile? :eyes:
sylvia: I grabbed a pprof at 30m into the run. Attaching the top lines below — looks like a lot of small allocations pinned to `kv/page.go:allocFragment` and some big ones in `batch/merge.go:mergeSlices`.

```
(pprof) top
Showing nodes accounting for 85.27MB, 100% of 85.27MB
      flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
    25.60MB 30.0% 30.0%     25.60MB 30.0%  kv/page.go:allocFragment
    18.40MB 21.6% 51.6%     43.20MB 50.7%  batch/merge.go:mergeSlices
    11.00MB 12.9% 64.5%     11.00MB 12.9%  runtime.mallocgc
     7.00MB  8.2% 72.7%      7.00MB  8.2%  kv/slot.go:markUsed

```

raj: That aligns with the trace I captured — continuous batching is consolidating requests, but when head-of-line (HOL) occurs because a live request expects an older KV layout, we split and re-alloc fragments instead of reusing. Leads to churn.

infra-bot: Deploy 2026-03-18T14:02:03 started by @sylvia: rollout/contbatch-opt-2026

sylvia: I also have a flame graph showing a hot path in `KVCache.GetFragment` calling `ensureCapacity` repeatedly during merges. If we don't reuse fragment buffers across splits, GC pressure climbs.
jun: Can you paste the minimal repro command? I can try a quick local run.

sylvia: repro: `./perf_harness --model long-context-65k --workload mixture --contbatch=on --seed 42 --duration 30m`

raj: Quick hack to test: toggle `batch.MergePolicy = PreferThinSlices` to avoid aggressive merges where KV layouts differ. Results: memory stops growing, but tail latency increases for small requests.

```
// config snippet
batch {
  continuous = true
  merge_policy = "prefer_thin_slices"
}
```

sylvia: Results from that run: peak RSS dropped ~18%, but p99 latency went from 120ms -> 230ms on short queries. So trade-off.

tess: We need a more surgical fix: either make fragments reusable across slightly different layouts or patch the merge path to avoid unnecessary splits.

raj: Another angle: add a fragmentation-aware LRU in KV pager so small fragments are coalesced before being evicted — reduces allocation storms when splits happen.

jun: I prototyped `fragmentPool` last week. Quick benchmark shows 40% fewer mallocs for merges when pool hitrate ~0.7. I'll push a branch and run the nightly.

sylvia: Please also add a diagnostic metric: `kv.fragment_reuse_rate` and `batch.merge_split_count`. We need visibility in Console before the next canary.

infra-bot: Metric `kv.fragment_reuse_rate` created by @jun

tess: Agreed. Priority: (1) add reuse pool + metrics, (2) instrument merge decision path, (3) run canary with long-context traffic. Leave continuous-batching on for canary but make merge policy adaptive.

raj: I'll file a lightweight RFC for the adaptive merge policy and include the pprof + flame results.

sylvia: Adding repro logs to the ticket. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
